passages.text: Now there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will secretly introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them—bringing swift destruction on themselves.
passages.sermon:
There were false prophets among the people in the past.
There will also be false teachers among you.
These false teachers will secretly bring in destructive heresies.
They will deny the Master who bought them.
They will bring swift destruction on themselves.
passages.original: Ἐγένοντο δὲ καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐν τῷ λαῷ ὡς καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσονται ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι οἵτινες παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας καὶ τὸν ἀγοράσαντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην ἀρνούμενοι ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν

passages.text: Many will follow in their depravity, and because of them the way of truth will be defamed.
passages.sermon:
Many people will follow these false teachers.
These people will imitate the immoral behavior of the false teachers.
Because of these followers, others will speak evil about the way of truth.
The way of truth means the true message from God.
People will dishonor and insult this true message because of the actions of these followers.
passages.original: καὶ πολλοὶ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταῖς ἀσελγείαις δι’ οὓς ἡ ὁδὸς τῆς ἀληθείας βλασφημηθήσεται

passages.text: In their greed, these false teachers will exploit you with deceptive words. The longstanding verdict against them remains in force, and their destruction does not sleep.
passages.sermon:
False teachers will come among you.
These false teachers are greedy.
They will use deceptive words.
They will exploit you.
God has already judged them long ago.
This judgment is still active.
Their destruction is certain.
Their destruction does not rest or delay.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ πλαστοῖς λόγοις ὑμᾶς ἐμπορεύσονται οἷς τὸ κρίμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει

passages.text: For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but cast them deep into hell, placing them in chains of darkness to be held for judgment; if He did not spare the ancient world when He brought the flood on its ungodly people, but preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, among the eight; if He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to destruction, reducing them to ashes as an example of what is coming on the ungodly; and if He rescued Lot, a righteous man distressed by the depraved conduct of the lawless (for that righteous man, living among them day after day, was tormented in his righteous soul by the lawless deeds he saw and heard)— if all this is so, then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and to hold the unrighteous for punishment on the day of judgment.
passages.sermon:
God judges sin.
God did not spare the angels when they sinned.
God cast these angels deep into hell.
God put them in chains of darkness.
God keeps them there for judgment.
God did not spare the ancient world.
God brought a flood on the ungodly people of that time.
God saved Noah.
Noah was a preacher of righteousness.
God saved Noah and seven others.
God condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah.
God destroyed these cities by reducing them to ashes.
God made them an example for the ungodly who would come later.
God rescued Lot.
Lot was a righteous man.
Lot was distressed by the depraved conduct of lawless people.
Lot lived among them day after day.
Lot saw and heard their lawless deeds.
Lot’s righteous soul was tormented by these deeds.
The Lord knows how to rescue godly people from trials.
The Lord keeps the unrighteous for punishment.
God will punish them on the day of judgment.
passages.original: Εἰ γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ἀγγέλων ἁμαρτησάντων οὐκ ἐφείσατο ἀλλὰ σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τηρουμένους καὶ ἀρχαίου κόσμου οὐκ ἐφείσατο ἀλλὰ ὄγδοον Νῶε δικαιοσύνης κήρυκα ἐφύλαξεν κατακλυσμὸν κόσμῳ ἀσεβῶν ἐπάξας καὶ πόλεις Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρας τεφρώσας καταστροφῇ κατέκρινεν ὑπόδειγμα μελλόντων ἀσεβέσιν τεθεικώς καὶ δίκαιον Λὼτ καταπονούμενον ὑπὸ τῆς τῶν ἀθέσμων ἐν ἀσελγείᾳ ἀναστροφῆς ἐρρύσατο βλέμματι γὰρ καὶ ἀκοῇ ὁ δίκαιος ἐνκατοικῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας ψυχὴν δικαίαν ἀνόμοις ἔργοις ἐβασάνιζεν οἶδεν Κύριος εὐσεβεῖς ἐκ πειρασμοῦ ῥύεσθαι ἀδίκους δὲ εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως κολαζομένους τηρεῖν

passages.text: Such punishment is specially reserved for those who indulge the corrupt desires of the flesh and despise authority. Bold and self-willed, they are unafraid to slander glorious beings.
passages.sermon:
God reserves special punishment for certain people.
These people follow the corrupt desires of their flesh.
They despise authority.
They are bold.
They are self-willed.
They are not afraid to slander glorious beings.
passages.original: μάλιστα δὲ τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ πορευομένους καὶ κυριότητος καταφρονοῦντας τολμηταὶ αὐθάδεις δόξας οὐ τρέμουσιν βλασφημοῦντες

passages.text: Yet not even angels, though greater in strength and power, dare to bring such slanderous charges against them before the Lord.
passages.sermon: Angels are greater in strength and power than people.\r\nAngels do not bring slanderous accusations against these people before the Lord.\r\nAngels do not dare to judge them with blasphemy before God.
passages.original: ὅπου ἄγγελοι ἰσχύϊ καὶ δυνάμει μείζονες ὄντες οὐ φέρουσιν κατ’ αὐτῶν παρὰ Κυρίῳ βλάσφημον κρίσιν

passages.text: These men are like irrational animals, creatures of instinct, born to be captured and destroyed. They blaspheme in matters they do not understand, and like such creatures, they too will be destroyed.
passages.sermon:
These men act like irrational animals.
They follow only their instincts.
God created such animals to be caught and destroyed.
These men speak evil about things they do not understand.
They blaspheme in their ignorance.
God will destroy them just as He destroys such animals.
passages.original: Οὗτοι δέ ὡς ἄλογα ζῷα γεγεννημένα φυσικὰ εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθοράν ἐν οἷς ἀγνοοῦσιν βλασφημοῦντες ἐν τῇ φθορᾷ αὐτῶν καὶ φθαρήσονται

passages.text: The harm they will suffer is the wages of their wickedness. They consider it a pleasure to carouse in broad daylight. They are blots and blemishes, reveling in their deception as they feast with you.
passages.sermon:
These men act wickedly.
They will suffer harm as payment for their wickedness.
They think it is pleasure to indulge themselves in the daytime.
They are blots and blemishes.
They celebrate their own deception.
They feast together with you.
passages.original: ἀδικούμενοι μισθὸν ἀδικίας ἡδονὴν ἡγούμενοι τὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τρυφήν σπίλοι καὶ μῶμοι ἐντρυφῶντες ἐν ταῖς ἀπάταις αὐτῶν συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν

passages.text: Their eyes are full of adultery; their desire for sin is never satisfied; they seduce the unstable. They are accursed children with hearts trained in greed.
passages.sermon:
These men are false teachers.
They are accursed children.
Their eyes are full of adultery.
They always want to sin.
They never stop sinning.
They seduce people who are not firm in faith.
Their hearts are trained in greed.
passages.original: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες μεστοὺς μοιχαλίδος καὶ ἀκαταπαύστους ἁμαρτίας δελεάζοντες ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους καρδίαν γεγυμνασμένην πλεονεξίας ἔχοντες κατάρας τέκνα

passages.text: They have left the straight way and wandered off to follow the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wickedness.
passages.sermon:
These people once followed the right path.
They turned away from it.
They wandered from the truth.
They chose to follow the way of Balaam.
Balaam was the son of Beor.
Balaam loved to receive payment for doing wrong.
These people act like Balaam.
They seek reward through wickedness.
passages.original: Καταλιπόντες εὐθεῖαν ὁδὸν ἐπλανήθησαν ἐξακολουθήσαντες τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ τοῦ Βεώρ ὃς μισθὸν ἀδικίας ἠγάπησεν

passages.text: But he was rebuked for his transgression by a donkey, otherwise without speech, that spoke with a man’s voice and restrained the prophet’s madness.
passages.sermon:
Balaam was a prophet.
\r\nBalaam committed a transgression.
\r\nA donkey rebuked Balaam for his transgression.
\r\nThis donkey could not normally speak.
\r\nThe donkey spoke with a man’s voice.
\r\nThe donkey stopped Balaam’s madness.
passages.original: ἔλεγξιν δὲ ἔσχεν ἰδίας παρανομίας ὑποζύγιον ἄφωνον ἐν ἀνθρώπου φωνῇ φθεγξάμενον ἐκώλυσεν τὴν τοῦ προφήτου παραφρονίαν

passages.text: These men are springs without water and mists driven by a storm. Blackest darkness is reserved for them.
passages.sermon:
These men are false teachers.
They promise life but give nothing.
They are like springs without water.
They are like mists driven by a storm.
God has reserved the blackest darkness for them.
passages.original: Οὗτοί εἰσιν πηγαὶ ἄνυδροι καὶ ὁμίχλαι ὑπὸ λαίλαπος ἐλαυνόμεναι οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους τετήρηται

passages.text: With lofty but empty words, they appeal to the sensual passions of the flesh and entice those who are just escaping from others who live in error.
passages.sermon:
These men speak with lofty words.
Their words are empty.
They use these words to attract people.
They appeal to the sinful desires of the flesh.
They entice people through acts of sensuality.
They target those who are just escaping from others who live in error.
passages.original: ὑπέρογκα γὰρ ματαιότητος φθεγγόμενοι δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς ἀσελγείαις τοὺς ὀλίγως ἀποφεύγοντας τοὺς ἐν πλάνῃ ἀναστρεφομένους

passages.text: They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves to depravity. For a man is a slave to whatever has mastered him.
passages.sermon:
These men promise others freedom.
These men are false teachers.
These men are actually slaves to depravity.
Depravity controls them.
A person becomes a slave to whatever defeats him.
If something masters a person, that person becomes its slave.
passages.original: ἐλευθερίαν αὐτοῖς ἐπαγγελλόμενοι αὐτοὶ δοῦλοι ὑπάρχοντες τῆς φθορᾶς ᾧ γάρ τις ἥττηται τούτῳ καὶ δεδούλωται

passages.text: If indeed they have escaped the corruption of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, only to be entangled and overcome by it again, their final condition is worse than it was at first.
passages.sermon:
Some people escape the corruption of the world.
They do this through knowing our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
Later, they become entangled in the corruption again.
The corruption overcomes them.
Their final condition becomes worse than their first condition.
passages.original: Εἰ γὰρ ἀποφυγόντες τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ Σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τούτοις δὲ πάλιν ἐμπλακέντες ἡττῶνται γέγονεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔσχατα χείρονα τῶν πρώτων

passages.text: It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than to have known it and then to turn away from the holy commandment passed on to them.
passages.sermon:
Some people learn the way of righteousness.
They receive the holy commandment.
They know what is right.
Then they turn away from it.
It would have been better for them if they had never known the way of righteousness.
It would have been better for them if they had never received the holy commandment.
passages.original: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἦν αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπεγνωκέναι τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἢ ἐπιγνοῦσιν ὑποστρέψαι ἐκ τῆς παραδοθείσης αὐτοῖς ἁγίας ἐντολῆς

passages.text: Of them the proverbs are true: “A dog returns to its vomit,” and, “A sow that is washed goes back to her wallowing in the mud.”
passages.sermon:
This passage describes people who once escaped the corruption of the world through knowing Jesus Christ.
These people returned to their old sinful ways.
The proverbs about them are true.
A dog returns to its own vomit.
A washed sow goes back to wallowing in the mud.
passages.original: συμβέβηκεν αὐτοῖς τὸ τῆς ἀληθοῦς παροιμίας Κύων ἐπιστρέψας ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον ἐξέραμα καί Ὗς λουσαμένη εἰς κυλισμὸν βορβόρου
